results.title: Remember Momo Mami? Shark Tank India's 1st pitch secured Rs 75 lakh from Ashneer Grover, Aman Gupta and Vineeta Singh — where is it now?
results.content:
The decline in revenue was accompanied by lower expenses. Employee costs fell to Rs 17.34 lakh in FY25 from Rs 53.33 lakh in FY24. Other expenses also declined during the year.

According to data, the Bluepine Foods has raised total equity funding of about Rs 1.37 crore across two funding rounds. The company remains at the seed stage, with its last known valuation at Rs 4.69 crore.

The company's financial performance has changed significantly since its first year. Revenue increased from Rs 9.92 lakh in FY17 to Rs 1.67 crore in FY25, although the latest figure remains below the FY24 peak of Rs 2.06 crore.

Bluepine Foods has also remained profitable in every financial year since FY18, but its profit margins have remained small relative to its revenue. [...] At the time of its Shark Tank India appearance, the company was largely focused on supplying hotels, restaurants and other food-service businesses. Its pitch came with an ask of Rs 50 lakh for 5 percent equity, implying a valuation of Rs 10 crore.

The founders eventually secured Rs 75 lakh for 16 percent equity from Aman, Vineeta and Ashneer. The three sharks invested Rs 25 lakh each.

## Related Stories

Bluepine Foods had a modest beginning. According to financial data from Tracxn, the company reported revenue of Rs 9.92 lakh in FY17, its first financial year. Expenses stood at Rs 18.55 lakh, resulting in a net loss of Rs 8.61 lakh. [...] Bluepine Foods recorded its highest revenue in FY24. Revenue rose to Rs 2.06 crore from Rs 1.73 crore in FY23. Net profit also improved to Rs 2.48 lakh from almost breakeven in the previous year.

The company therefore recorded its strongest revenue and profit numbers in FY24.

However, the growth did not continue into the following financial year.

Bluepine Foods' revenue declined in FY25. Tracxn data shows that revenue fell to Rs 1.67 crore from Rs 2.06 crore in FY24, a decline of about 19 percent.

Profitability also weakened sharply. Net profit dropped to Rs 24 thousand in FY25 from Rs 2.48 lakh a year earlier.

The company's EBITDA remained positive at Rs 10.53 lakh during FY25.

### The Deal: From Pitch to Handshake

The negotiation was a masterclass in founder conviction. After receiving multiple offers and counter-offers, the team secured a joint deal from three Sharks who saw the brand’s potential. [...] Bluepine Foods: Paneer Momos

#### Key Takeaways for Entrepreneurs

The journey of Bluepine Foods offers several powerful lessons for aspiring founders:

 Product is King: The unanimous praise for the product’s taste was the foundation of the deal. A great product can overcome doubts in other areas.
 Know Your Numbers: The founders’ command of their sales figures and business model gave the Sharks confidence in their ability to execute.
 Be Flexible, But Stand Firm: The team was willing to negotiate on equity but stood firm on their vision, ultimately securing a better deal than their initial ask.

BluePine Foods is a food startup specializing in frozen momo and dumplings, focusing on Himalayan cuisine. BluePine Foods serves the HORECA sector with customizable food products. It was founded in 2016 and is based in Faridabad, India.
